title: The Dune Line
intro_lines: Your tongue feels like a boot sole.
Tide-Puck paws at the sand behind the dune.
Salt everywhere. Not a drop to drink.

choices.label: Dig behind the dune line

outcomes.text: Brackish water seeps into the hole. It tastes of iron and mud, but it stays down.
The hole collapses. You drink a mouthful of grit and salt, and your head pounds harder.

choices.label: Build a solar still from sailcloth

outcomes.text: By dusk the cloth has beaded. Half a cup, warm and flat. You give Tide-Puck a lick.
A gull tears the cloth loose. You salvage the clear sheet and little else.
The still works better than you feared. A full cup by noon, and a second by dusk.

choices.label: Crack green coconuts

outcomes.text: The water is sweet and cool. Too much will loosen your gut, so you ration it.
The nut is old and sour. You retch into the sand and your throat burns.

choices.label: Squeeze moisture from fish flesh

outcomes.text: You chew the raw flesh and wring the pulp into a shell. It is foul, but it is wet.
The fish is half rotten. You gag it down and spend the afternoon doubled over.

history_note: Digging behind the dune line for a brackish freshwater lens and drinking green coconut water in moderation were real castaway water strategies, while NOAA warns that seawater only worsens dehydration.

title: A Spark in the Wet
intro_lines: Rain has soaked every scrap of tinder.
Your knife and a shard of flint are all you have.
Tide-Puck sneezes at the wet ash.

choices.label: Strike flint on the knife spine

outcomes.text: A spark catches in coconut-husk fibre. You cup it like a live thing and feed it.
Sparks hiss and die. Your knuckles are raw and the tinder is grey pulp.
The flint slips. The blade opens your thumb to the bone and the tinder is bloodied.

choices.label: Shield the tinder from the squall

outcomes.text: The rain passes. Dry husk fibre, a steady spark, and flame at last.
Hours lost. The cold settles into your shoulders and you cannot stop shaking.

choices.label: Keep the old ember in a shell

outcomes.text: The shell shields the coal from the wind. You feed it driftwood and breathe it back.
The shell splits in the heat. The coal dies with it and you are left with ash.

history_note: The Tromelin castaways used flint strikers left by the French crew until the stones were worn to nothing.

title: Green-Black Sky
intro_lines: The wind shifts and the sky goes green-black.
Your scrap shelter will not survive this.

choices.label: Build a coral-stone windbreak

outcomes.text: You stack beachrock shoulder-high and brace it with wreck planks. The storm screams past.
The wall stands, but the rain finds you. You spend the night hunched and shivering.

choices.label: Lash sailcloth over a lean-to

outcomes.text: The canvas holds. You sleep dry for the first time in days and wake almost warm.
A gust tears the canvas from the frame. You chase it into the surf and lose it.

choices.label: Dig into the sand and let it bury you

outcomes.text: Sand insulates better than you expected. You wake stiff and gritty, but alive.
Water runs into the hole. You spend the night soaked, teeth chattering, eyes open.

history_note: Tromelin's survivors built 1.5 m thick coral-and-beachrock walls with their backs to the trade wind after a storm destroyed their shelters.

title: The Fat Grouper
intro_lines: You speared a fat grouper on the reef.
Tide-Puck refuses to touch it, whining.

choices.label: Roast it whole and eat your fill

outcomes.text: Rich, oily, filling. For an hour you are the richest man on this island.
By dusk your lips tingle and hot and cold have swapped places. Ciguatera.
You eat half and bury the rest. Your gut twists hard, then holds.

choices.label: Feed a strip to Tide-Puck first

outcomes.text: The puck sniffs, gags, and turns away. You bury the fish and eat shellfish instead.
Tide-Puck eats it, then retches for hours. You feel like a monster.

choices.label: Eat only the small reef fish

outcomes.text: Small wrasses and damsels, grilled hot. Plain, safe, and enough.
One of them was not as small as you thought. Your stomach turns by dark.

history_note: Big reef predators such as grouper and barracuda carry ciguatera toxin that cooking does not destroy, so islanders learned to eat small reef fish.

title: Coral Crest
intro_lines: A wave shoves you onto the reef crest.
Your shin is laid open on the coral.

choices.label: Rinse it in the sea and bind it tight

outcomes.text: You pack the cut with crushed herbs and wrap it tight. It throbs, but it holds.
By morning the edges are red and hot. The wound is turning and the leg is stiff.

choices.label: Cauterise the cut with a firebrand

outcomes.text: The pain is white and total, but the bleeding stops and the flesh seals.
The brand slips. You burn healthy skin and the wound weeps worse than before.

choices.label: Chew a herb poultice and rest

outcomes.text: The swelling goes down by the second day. You keep the leg and the lesson.
Fever takes you. You hallucinate ships and wake to Tide-Puck licking your face.

history_note: NOAA reef-hazard guidance stresses that coral cuts infect fast and urchin spines lodge deep, so prompt cleaning and rest matter more than bravado.

title: A Sail Past the Shoals
intro_lines: A sail, white as a gull's wing, on the horizon.
It is heading past the shoals.
It will not see you.

choices.label: Light three fires in a triangle

outcomes.text: Green leaves make a fat white column. The sail changes course. A boat is lowered.
The fires burn, but the ship holds its line. Dusk swallows the sail entirely.
A squall kills the fires before the smoke can rise. The horizon empties.

choices.label: Flash a mirror from the cliff

outcomes.text: A pinpoint of sun stabs across the water. The ship answers with a lamp and a launch turns.
The glare is lost in the swell. Your arms ache and the sail passes on.

choices.label: Swim out and wave

outcomes.text: You make the breakers. A lookout spots you and a line is thrown across the swell.
The current drags you under twice. You crawl back to the sand, lungs burning.
Something bumps your leg in the deep water. You turn back fast and do not look.

history_note: Castaways signalled with three fires in a triangle and green leaves for white smoke, yet ships often avoided dangerous shoals and ignored smoke, as Pedro Serrano discovered.

title: The Large Quiet
intro_lines: The dark is very large and very quiet.
You have started talking to Tide-Puck.
You cannot remember your own voice.

choices.label: Keep a tally and a journal on a plank

outcomes.text: Scratches on wood become days, and days become a plan. The dread loosens its grip.
The tally fills you with the size of the emptiness. You stop counting and sit.

choices.label: Ration the rum and drink to the crew

outcomes.text: One mouthful, then the bottle corked. The warmth is borrowed, but it helps.
You drink too deep. Morning finds you sick, salt-mouthed and ashamed.

choices.label: Walk the tideline to keep moving

outcomes.text: You walk until your legs ache. Sleep comes without dreams for once.
The dark plays tricks. Every stump is a ship, every bird a shout. You run.

choices.label: Read aloud from the torn map

outcomes.text: Names of places you have never seen. Your voice sounds strange and steady.
The names blur. You realise you have read the same line six times.

history_note: Alexander Selkirk read the Bible aloud to keep his speech and tamed cats for company, routines that castaway accounts credit with holding despair at bay.

title: A Raft at Dawn
intro_lines: A raft grinds onto the reef at dawn.
One man aboard, half-dead, salt-crusted.
He clutches a UTC water skin.

choices.label: Share water and hear him out

outcomes.text: He drinks, then weeps. His name is Cobb, a deserter off a UTC tender.
He drinks and says nothing. His eyes keep drifting to your stores.

choices.label: Bind him and take the water skin

outcomes.text: You take his skin and tie his wrists. He smiles at you, which is worse.
He fights like a drowning man. You win, but he splits your brow open.

choices.label: Drive him back into the sea

outcomes.text: You shove the raft off. He curses you in three languages and drifts away.
He refuses to go. You stand over him with a spar until he crawls off.

history_note: Castaways face a rough order of threats: about 3 hours of exposure, 3 days without water, 3 weeks without food.

title: Cobb Earns His Keep
intro_lines: Cobb works without being asked.
He knows the reef, the tides, the UTC signals.
Too well, perhaps.

choices.label: Let him teach you the UTC signal code

outcomes.text: Flags, lamps, the shape of a patrol's hull. You will see them coming now.
He teaches you wrong on purpose, or you only suspect it. A wasted day.

choices.label: Send him to scout the far headland

outcomes.text: He returns with a map fragment and a cut on his arm. He does not say whose.
He comes back empty-handed and evasive. Something on that headland frightened him.

choices.label: Search his sea chest while he sleeps

outcomes.text: Under a false bottom: a UTC dark-binding crystal, wrapped in oilcloth.
He wakes. Neither of you speaks. The knife lies on the sand between you.

history_note: A deserter told Bartholomew Roberts how HMS Swallow sailed best, and pirate crews routinely took skilled men for the knowledge they carried.

title: What Cobb Really Wants
intro_lines: You wake to the sound of your water gourds moving.
Cobb is at the stores with your knife.

choices.label: Put the blade to his throat

outcomes.text: He drops the skin and begs. You let him live, and he never sleeps easy again.
He is faster than he looked. The knife goes into your shoulder to the hilt.
You drive him off the reef at spear-point. He curses until the surf takes him.

choices.label: Let him take the water and follow

outcomes.text: He leads you to a tideborn arch with a fresh spring. He knew, and he was thirsty too.
He leads you into a UTC patrol's lantern light. You run. He does not.

choices.label: Bar the cave mouth and wait for dawn

outcomes.text: You wedge the entrance with wreck timber. By dawn he is gone, and half your food.
He sets the bar alight. You drag the stores out through the smoke and lose some.

history_note: In the heat and rain, Pedro Serrano's provisions spoiled within two months; meat had to be dried in the sun to last.

title: A Second Voice
intro_lines: Smoke on the western headland.
Someone else survived the wreck.
They wave a torn sail.

choices.label: Signal with three fires

outcomes.text: They pole a raft across the channel, weak but grateful. Shared rations buy trust.
They fear the Sovereign and refuse to cross; the smoke dies by dusk.
The signal draws a UTC longboat instead; you scatter into the scrub.

choices.label: Keep your distance

outcomes.text: They vanish into the jungle. You stay alive, and alone.
They leave a crate of salt pork on the rocks at dawn. No note.

history_note: Pedro Serrano shared his cay with a second castaway; they quarrelled, then reconciled.

title: Stranger's Fire
intro_lines: The stranger limps into camp.
Fever in his eyes, hands raw.
He asks for water, then silence.

choices.label: Nurse him with coconut water

outcomes.text: The fever breaks by morning. He swears an oath to your crew.
He recovers, but eyes your stores. Trust is thin.

choices.label: Turn him out before dawn

outcomes.text: He staggers off. Your stores stay yours, and your conscience.
He returns at night with two UTC privateers. You flee.

history_note: Selkirk tamed kid goats for company; isolation warps judgement of strangers.

title: Betrayal or Bond
intro_lines: He finds the relic shard cache.
Says he'll tell UTC for a pardon.
Your hand on your cutlass.

choices.label: Offer him a share of the haul

outcomes.text: He takes the share, and later drags a wounded tideborn scout to safety. Bonded.
He takes the share, vanishes at dusk with your best knife.

choices.label: Maroon him with water and powder

outcomes.text: Articles upheld. He curses you from the rocks, then goes quiet.
He signals a passing sloop; UTC learns your camp's position.

history_note: Roberts' articles punished defrauding the company with marooning and a bottle of water.

title: Black Gums and Bleeding
intro_lines: Your gums bleed when you chew.
Old scars reopen, slow to close.
Scurvy's grip tightens.

choices.label: Hunt greens and fruit

outcomes.text: Tide-Puck sniffs out a patch of wild cabbage palm. Chewing restores you.
You find only manchineel; the rash keeps you from eating.
A boar charges from the undergrowth; you flee with nothing.

choices.label: Chew hide and drink coconut water

outcomes.text: The hide sits heavy; coconut water eases the thirst but not the sores.
The vitamin-starved body worsens; you collapse at dusk.

history_note: Scurvy struck sailors without fresh greens; Ada Blackjack nursed Lorne Knight until he died.

title: Rotting Stores
intro_lines: The salt pork has gone green.
Maggots in the biscuit barrel.
Heat and rain have won.

choices.label: Smoke and dry what you can

outcomes.text: You salvage half the meat over a slow fire. The rest feeds the crabs.
The fire flares; you scorch the lot. Smoke billows, and gulls come.

choices.label: Eat it raw and risk it

outcomes.text: Your gut holds. The protein buys a day of strength.
Cramps and fever by midnight. You crawl to the beach.

history_note: In the heat and rain, Pedro Serrano's provisions spoiled within two months; meat had to be dried in the sun to last.

title: Coral Cut Gone Wrong
intro_lines: A coral cut on your shin.
It's red, hot, swelling fast.
The reef has teeth.

choices.label: Clean with fresh water and herbs

outcomes.text: The swelling fades. You keep the leg, and your footing.
Infection lingers; you limp for days but survive.

choices.label: Urinate on it and bind with cloth

outcomes.text: It stings, but the wound seals. Old sailor's trick.
Fever sets in by nightfall. You shiver on the sand.

history_note: Coral cuts infect fast in tropical heat; NOAA lists reef hazards among castaway dangers.

title: Talking to the Wind
intro_lines: You catch yourself arguing aloud.
Tide-Puck tilts its head, listening.
The silence is eating you.

choices.label: Keep a daily tally and read aloud

outcomes.text: The routine steadies you. Speech stays sharp. Hope flickers.
The journal soaks in a squall. You start again, stubborn.

choices.label: Drink rum and sleep through it

outcomes.text: A heavy, dreamless sleep. You wake hollow but rested.
You wake shouting at nothing. Tide-Puck hides for hours.

history_note: Selkirk read the Bible aloud to keep his speech; routines guard the mind.

title: One Fire, Fifteen Years
intro_lines: The rain soaks every tinder.
One ember left in the hearth.
If it dies, you start over.

choices.label: Shield it and feed dry husk

outcomes.text: The flame holds. Warmth and smoke through the night.
A gust snuffs it. You spend hours with the bow drill.

choices.label: Let it die, relight at dawn

outcomes.text: You sleep. At dawn the bow drill catches on the third try.
Humid air defeats the drill. Cold and dark till noon.

history_note: Tromelin's castaways kept one fire alive fifteen years; flint strikers wore to nothing.

title: Smoke on the Horizon
intro_lines: Three fires in a triangle.
A sloop passes, then turns away.
They fear the shoals.

choices.label: Add green leaves for white smoke

outcomes.text: The white column climbs. The sloop hesitates, then sails on.
The smoke draws a tideborn scout instead. They watch, then vanish.

choices.label: Flash a mirror from the cliff

outcomes.text: A glint back. They lower a boat, then abort. Shoals win.
UTC privateers answer the flash. You duck into the cave.

history_note: Serrano's smoke was ignored by ships afraid of the shoals; signalling is no guarantee.

title: Night Rain Catchment
intro_lines: Rain drums the palm fronds.
Empty shells and a torn sail.
Water or nothing tonight.

choices.label: Rig sailcloth as a funnel

outcomes.text: Gallons pour into the basins. Clean water for days.
The wind tears the cloth; you salvage a trickle.

choices.label: Line shells and coconut husks

outcomes.text: A modest catch. Enough to stave off the thirst.
Dust and grit ruin half of it. You drink anyway.

history_note: Serrano used shells as rain catchers, holding up to twelve gallons.

title: The Last Turtle
intro_lines: A green turtle hauls ashore.
Moonlight on her shell.
She's heavy, and she's yours.

choices.label: Flip her and save for morning

outcomes.text: She's on her back by dawn. Meat, shell, and oil for weeks.
She rights herself in the night and slips away.

choices.label: Kill and butcher at once

outcomes.text: Fresh meat tonight. You salt the rest before it spoils.
Blood draws a reef shark into the shallows. You retreat.

history_note: Serrano flipped sea turtles onto their backs and drank their blood when no rain fell.
